body:
_Migrated from issue #1388, filed 2026-08-05._

The follow-up board's "We owe a reply" section decides someone is waiting on us purely from *who* commented last, never from *what* they said. Measured against all 8 rows on the 2026-08-05T02:07Z board, 5 are not owed anything:

| Thread | Last comment | Actually owed? |
|---|---|---|
| #1229, #1054, #947 | substantive feedback, unanswered | yes |
| #1253 | reporter solved it themselves and posted the workaround for others | no |
| #997 | "Thanks for the merge, I'll follow this!" | no |
| #509, #304 | "I'll test and let you know" — ball is in their court | no |
| #705 | "I can confirm that I can hide the discovery section using the new UI." | no — this is a **verification** |

The predicate, `scripts/gen-followup-board.sh:160`:

```
owe_reply: (
    (.last_comment != null)
    and (.last_comment.author.login != $self)
    and (secs_since(.last_comment.createdAt) > 172800)
    and (.has_awaiting | not)
)
```

#705 is the case worth fixing. @kdbruin confirmed the fix works on 2026-07-28 and it has sat in "we owe a reply" for 8 days since. Under the shipping policy a reporter's confirmation is the close trigger, so this should have closed a week ago.

The reason it hid is the last clause composing with the auto-close sweep. When a reporter engages, `auto-close-awaiting-verification.sh` removes the `awaiting-verification` label — correctly, their engagement did its job. But that removal is exactly what makes `(.has_awaiting | not)` true, so the issue moves out of "Awaiting reporter" and into "We owe a reply", where a confirmation looks identical to a complaint. **Confirming a fix is what disguises the issue as a debt**, which is the one signal the board most needs to not lose.

Worth being precise about scope: the structural predicate is doing something valuable — it cannot miss a waiting user, and false positives are far cheaper than false negatives on this board. The fix is not to make it cleverer, it is to classify the rows it produces.

Suggested shape:

1. Run the existing semantic classifier over `owe_reply` rows, not just `awaiting-verification` ones. `verification-sweep.sh` already calls Gemini for exactly this judgment (confirmation / pushback / partial) and reported `0 threads with something new to read` this tick because its input set excludes these. Widening the input set reuses the whole mechanism.
2. Give a classified confirmation its own board section, or close it directly per the shipping policy.
3. Keep the unclassified default in "We owe a reply" — an unread row must stay visible, never be silently dropped.

Not urgent at 8 rows, but this is the failure mode that just cost the untriaged section its usefulness: a section whose majority is noise stops being read, and the row that meant a real person was waiting goes with it. At 62% noise this section is already past that line.
title: Follow-up board files reporter confirmations as "we owe a reply" (5 of 8 rows are not owed)
